entries.title: What is Kindle Mode on the new Alexa Tablets?
entries.summary: What is Kindle Mode, which is available on all new Amazon Alexa Tablets? We break down all of the new features and what they do. The post What is Kindle Mode on the new Alexa Tablets? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
A few weeks ago, Amazon announced a new line of tablets called Alexa. They have Android 16 and have full access to the Google Play Store. This is the first time Amazon has done this; in the past, it ran FireOS and only had the Amazon App Store, which lacked mainstream apps. One feature on Alexa tablets is called Kindle Mode; what is it, and what does it do?

Kindle Mode

Kindle Mode activates automatically whenever you open a book inside the native Kindle app. The moment you exit your book or close the app, the tablet immediately reverts to its normal Android tablet interface and standard display settings. When you enter Kindle Mode, the system triggers several background changes designed to mimic a dedicated e-reader

The first new thing that Kindle Mode provides is a distraction-free sanctuary: It silences and mutes all incoming notifications automatically so you can focus entirely on your book. It reduces blue light; the screen shifts to a lower, warmer color temperature that is much softer on the eyes. It limits background processes, stretching the tablet’s battery life up to 20 hours of continuous reading.

One of the standout features is called display profiles. You can customize the look to match your reading material, switching between a classic grayscale look (simulating traditional paper), a soft muted color layout, or a vivid glossy profile suited for magazines and comics.

Kindle Mode is only compatible with the new Amazon Alexa Tablet 8, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. Android Police wrote an excellent article on how to replicate it on Samsung Galaxy tablets.

entries.title: Amazon Kindle Oasis back in stock in the United States
entries.summary: The Amazon Kindle Oasis is back in stock on Amazon for a limited time. They are new, not refurbished, and are reasonably priced. The post Amazon Kindle Oasis back in stock in the United States first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Amazon Kindle Oasis is back in stock for a limited time on the main Amazon.com website in the United States. The Graphite model with 8GB of storage is $115, the Oasis Graphite model with 32GB of storage is $145, and the Champagne Gold model with 32GB is $144. These prices are very good; considering the last time the 8GB model was in stock, it cost over $178.00.

All Kindle Oasis models that are back in stock are new, not refurbished or returned. This means you will get a brand-new one, still in the original packaging. The Oasis remains one of Amazon’s most-regarded e-readers because it was the last to have physical page-turn buttons.

The Kindle Oasis 3 features a 7-inch E Ink Carta HD capacitive touchscreen display with a resolution of 1680 x 1264 and 300 PPI. The screen is glass, and the body is high-grade aluminum. It has a front-lit display and is the first Kindle with a color temperature system. The front-lit display and color system can both be controlled by slider bars in the quick settings menu, or can automatically be adjusted based on the time of day via the ambient light sensor. It has 25 LED lights total, 12 white and 13 amber.

Underneath the hood is a Freescale/NXP IMX7 dual-core 1 GHZ processor with 512 MB of RAM. The Oasis keeps the two manual page-turn buttons on the right side of the screen, and the settings menu lets you reverse the page turns, so up is down and down is up, which is ideal for manga. This is the only Kindle model that has physical page turn buttons. If you hold the e-reader in one hand while reading an ebook, you can disable the touchscreen; this is useful on public transit.

If you love reading in the bathtub or at the beach, the Kindle Oasis 3 is waterproof. It is certified IPX8 to protect against immersion in up to two meters of freshwater, for up to 60 minutes. If your Kindle is splashed with water, wipe it off with a soft cloth and keep on reading. If your Kindle is immersed in water, remove its cover, make sure no cables are plugged into the device, and do not attempt to charge your Kindle until it is completely dry. If your Kindle is immersed in salt water, chlorinated water, soapy water, or liquids other than fresh water, make sure you rinse that liquid out of the device with fresh water such as cold tap water. Then dry your Kindle.

Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons

  • Our best 7", 300 ppi flush-front Paperwhite display.
  • Adjustable warm light to shift screen shade from white to amber.
  • Waterproof (IPX8) so you can read in the bath or by the pool. Your Kindle has been tested to withstand accidental immersion in water.

entries.title: All of the new 2026 Kindles have user replaceable batteries
entries.summary: All of the new 2026 Amazon Kindle e-readers made of plastic or aluminum have user-replaceable batteries. Battery Health can be viewed in the settings menu, and a QR code takes you to battery replacements. The post All of the new 2026 Kindles have user replaceable batteries first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
All of the latest-generation Amazon Kindle e-readers have user-replaceable batteries. This includes the new Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite, Paperwhite Signature Edition, Kindle Colorsoft, and the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition. There is this new Amazon Kindle Battery Guide page that was recently added to the help section of Amazon’s website.

With Amazon’s freshly redesigned 2026 Kindle lineup, replacing the battery has become significantly easier. Driven by upcoming European Union regulations, Amazon built these models with a removable, user-replaceable back panel (EBR-compliant), entirely shifting away from the tightly glued-shut designs of previous generations. Depending on whether you have a standard plastic model or an upgraded aluminum variant, accessing and swapping the battery differs slightly.

The plastic models tend to pop off very easily, since there are no screws. All you need is your fingernail, a guitar pick, or something similar. Remove the battery by unscrewing the four Phillips-head screws securing it to the frame. On Kindles with an aluminum backplate, remove two tiny hex screws on the bottom edge of the device. Then pry it open with a fingernail, guitar pick, or something similar.

View battery health

The 2026 Amazon Kindle e-readers all have a new battery health system. You can check your device’s current health directly by navigating to Settings > Device options > Battery > Battery information. The device will flag if it is running normally, has limited capacity, or recognizes an incompatible third-party cell. Amazon includes QR codes directly within the device firmware interface that link to approved battery replacement kits and official replacement instructions.

entries.title: Kobo Plus Audiobooks now available in France
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo Audiobooks are now available in France. You can listen to content on the Kobo apps and e-readers. The post Kobo Plus Audiobooks now available in France first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Kobo Plus is fully available in France, offering a flexible subscription service for book lovers. Originally launched in France in partnership with Fnac in November 2021, the service has recently expanded its catalog to include both digital books and audiobooks. Rakuten Kobo has just announced that audiobooks are now available too.

With a vast selection of more than 2 million eBooks and over 500,000 audiobooks available through Kobo Plus, French readers can choose between a read-only plan for €9.99 per month or opt for the combined read and listen subscription for €14.99 per month. With a 14-day free trial, readers can enjoy access to the entire Kobo Plus catalog and discover their next favorite read, commitment-free.

“Our goal at Rakuten Kobo is to make reading lives better, and enhancing the Kobo Plus experience for our French readers is an important step forward in that mission,” said Bart Robers, Senior Director of Audiobooks and Global Subscriptions, Rakuten Kobo. “Since bringing our read-only subscription to France in 2021, it has been inspiring to witness the passion and voracity for literature among French readers, which is why we are expanding our Kobo Plus offering to include audiobooks. This expansion provides another convenient way for book lovers to enjoy their favorite stories while on the move.”

Readers can choose from two flexible plans:

Kobo Plus Read – Access to millions of eBooks for a monthly cost of 9.99 EUR

Kobo Plus Read & Listen – The perfect combination for those who enjoy eBooks and audiobooks, for a monthly cost of only 14.99 EUR

entries.title: As More Books Move Online, CZUR Book Scanners Help Preserve Printed Information
entries.summary: Factories rely on technical manuals and reference books, researchers need older editions… The post As More Books Move Online, CZUR Book Scanners Help Preserve Printed Information first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Factories rely on technical manuals and reference books, researchers need older editions that may not be available online, and businesses still maintain paper contracts, invoices, and historical records. Digitizing these materials makes them easier to access, search, and preserve, especially when large volumes of documents need to be processed.

However, scanning a thick textbook, a fragile historical book, or a glossy magazine is not always straightforward. Traditional flatbed scanners work well for loose sheets, but bound books present additional challenges. Pages may curve near the spine, text can become distorted, and pressing a book flat may damage its binding.

An overhead book scanner offers a practical alternative. By capturing pages from above rather than pressing them against a glass surface, it can make digitizing bound materials easier and less physically demanding. For libraries, researchers, educators, and businesses, the right scanning equipment can help turn printed resources into more accessible digital files.

Why Bound Books Need a Different Scanning Approach

Scanning a bound book with a conventional flatbed scanner can be frustrating. The binding prevents pages from lying completely flat, creating shadows and distortion around the spine. This can make text near the center of an open book difficult to read, particularly when working with thick volumes.

Overhead book scanners are designed to address these challenges. The CZUR ET series, for example, uses laser-assisted curve flattening technology to detect page curvature and help correct distortion through its software. Automatic tilt correction helps straighten misaligned images, while the page-splitting function separates the left and right pages of an open book into individual digital pages.

These features can reduce the amount of manual image correction needed after scanning. They are particularly useful when digitizing textbooks, reference materials, and other bound publications that would be inconvenient to process one page at a time on a flatbed scanner.

The results will still depend on the condition of the book, its layout, and the scanning settings. However, for people who regularly work with bound materials, an overhead scanner can offer a more convenient workflow.

From Scanned Images to Searchable Documents

Capturing a page is only the first step in digitization. A folder of scanned images may preserve the appearance of a book, but finding a particular passage can still mean opening files one by one and reading through the pages.

Optical character recognition (OCR) helps solve this problem by identifying printed characters in scanned images and converting them into machine-readable text. Depending on the software and output format, users can search for keywords, copy passages, and export recognized text into editable documents.

CZUR ET series scanners support OCR through compatible scanning software, including ABBYY-based technology. Supported export formats and editing capabilities vary by model and software version, so it is worth checking the specifications before purchasing.

Searchable digital files can make a substantial difference in everyday work. Researchers can locate relevant passages without repeatedly browsing entire books, students can organize academic references more efficiently, and businesses can retrieve information from archived paperwork more easily.

OCR does have limitations. Faded printing, unusual fonts, curved text, and complex page layouts can reduce recognition accuracy. Scanned documents containing important figures, dates, or technical information should therefore be checked before the recognized text is used.

What Affects Scanning Speed and Image Quality?

When scanning a few pages, speed may not be a major concern. When the task involves dozens of books or hundreds of pages, however, even small differences in processing time can add up.

The CZUR ET series includes models designed for relatively fast page capture. For example, the ET Max is rated at approximately 1.5 seconds per page under suitable conditions. Actual processing time may vary depending on the scanning mode, page layout, and software workflow. Image processing and OCR may also require additional time.

Lighting is another important consideration, particularly when working with glossy magazines, coated paper, or materials with uneven surfaces. Reflections can obscure text or details in a captured image, making it harder to read or recognize the content.

Some CZUR ET models include adjustable LED lighting, and the ET Max features angled side lighting designed to help manage reflections. Appropriate lighting can improve image quality, although it cannot eliminate every reflection. For challenging materials, it is still worth testing different lighting positions and settings before scanning an entire collection.

Resolution also matters when fine print, illustrations, or small details need to be preserved. The CZUR ET Max, for instance, features a 38-megapixel camera and a default optical resolution of 410 DPI. Other ET models have different specifications, so these figures should not be treated as representative of the entire series.

Who Can Benefit From Book Scanning?

Overhead book scanners are particularly useful for people who regularly work with bound publications or large collections of printed information.

  • Libraries and archives: Digitize selected reference books, older publications, and archival materials while retaining the physical originals. Digital copies can make frequently consulted resources easier to access.
  • Researchers and academics: Create searchable copies of reference materials, older editions, and printed sources that may be difficult to find online.
  • Schools and universities: Digitize selected teaching materials, lecture notes, and reference pages for easier organization and retrieval, subject to applicable copyright and distribution rules.
  • Businesses and offices: Convert paper records, contracts, invoices, certificates, and manuals into digital files that are easier to search and organize.

A dedicated book scanner is not necessary for everyone. If you only scan receipts or occasional loose documents, a smartphone scanning app or a conventional document scanner may be sufficient.

A specialized overhead scanner makes more sense when book scanning is a regular task, the materials are bound or difficult to flatten, and preserving the original pages is important.

How to Choose the Right CZUR Book Scanner

Not every scanning project requires the same equipment. Before choosing a scanner, consider the types of materials you handle, how frequently you scan, and what you need to do with the resulting files.

Here are several factors worth comparing:

  • Page size: Check whether the scanner accommodates the dimensions of your books and documents. A3 support can be useful for larger publications.
  • Camera resolution: Higher resolution can help capture fine print and detailed images, although the final result also depends on focus, lighting, and processing.
  • Page flattening and correction: If you frequently scan thick or tightly bound books, curve correction and automatic tilt correction can reduce manual adjustments.
  • OCR and export options: Confirm which languages, file formats, and editable document functions are supported by the specific model and software.
  • Scanning speed: Consider the number of pages you process regularly, rather than relying on the advertised capture speed alone.
  • Software compatibility: Verify that the scanning software supports your operating system and required workflow.

The CZUR ET lineup includes several models, such as the ET Max, ET24 Pro, ET18 Pro, and ET16 Plus. Their camera specifications, resolution, and other capabilities differ, so the right choice depends on your requirements rather than the model name alone.

For users handling thick books, large reference volumes, or frequent scanning projects, the CZUR ET Max book scanner offers a combination of overhead capture, laser-assisted curve flattening, OCR support, and fast page capture. Its 38-megapixel camera, 410 DPI default optical resolution, and A3 scanning capacity make it one option worth considering for these tasks.

Before purchasing, test a few representative pages if possible. Include the most challenging materials in your collection, such as tightly bound books, small print, or glossy pages. This will give you a more realistic idea of the image quality and amount of post-processing required.

Making Printed Information Easier to Preserve and Use

Printed books and paper records remain important across education, research, libraries, and business. Digitization helps make these resources easier to find and use, but bound materials often require a different approach from loose sheets.

Overhead book scanners can simplify the process by capturing pages without requiring them to be pressed against a glass bed. Features such as curve correction, OCR, and automatic image processing can further reduce the effort involved in turning printed information into usable digital files.

A scanner alone, however, cannot replace quality checks, a well-organized filing system, reliable backups, or attention to copyright requirements. Choosing equipment that matches your materials and workflow is what makes digitization worthwhile.

For anyone who regularly works with bound books and printed records, a suitable book scanner can help preserve valuable information while making it easier to search, organize, and access in digital form.

Markus lives in San Francisco, California and is the video game and audio expert on Good e-Reader! He has a huge interest in new e-readers and tablets, and gaming.

entries.title: E-Reader companies are slow to adopt Android 16
entries.summary: Google Android 16 is the latest version of the OS that is slowly starting to see minor adoption in e-readers and e-notebooks. Will we see a wider variety in 2027? The post E-Reader companies are slow to adopt Android 16 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E-readers running Google Android are plentiful, but hardly any run a modern version of Android. Android 16 is the latest version being slowly adopted, and only the Viwoods AiPaper, BOOX Palma 3, Note Air6 C, and Boox Note Mini C run it. A few E-ink smartphones also run Android 16, such as the Bigme HiBreak Dual 2 / Dual 3 and the Hisense A10 series.

Android 16 brings a modern base operating system to modern E-Ink devices, focusing on better app compatibility, integrated artificial intelligence, and improved hardware performance. Unlike older, locked-down or outdated Android-based e-readers, Android 16 devices offer broad compatibility with modern third-party apps, allowing you to install Kindle, Kobo, Google Play Books, and productivity or news apps seamlessly. Viwoods and BOOX models ship with native or bundled AI tools—such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek—built right into the system or side-key shortcuts for on-page text summaries, translation, and document analysis.

It remains to be seen if 2027 will have a wider variety of e-readers with Android 16 and full access to the Google Play Store. Viwoods, Bigme, and BOOX will likely have more devices, and more regional players will enter the market. The Barnes and Noble NOOK runs Android, but they tend to skin it in such a way that you would never know it. They plan a few new devices in 2027; it is not out of the question that they’ll use a modern OS. Pocketbook also has a few models with Android and Google Play, but it is more of a small foray than a new company direction.

entries.title: Everything you need to know about E INK Kaleido 4
entries.summary: E INK Kaleido 4 was just announced with 300 PPI for color content and a 50% improvement in contrast ratio. Look for new Kobo, NOOK, Onyx Boox, and Bigme products in early 2027. The post Everything you need to know about E INK Kaleido 4 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E Ink has announced its next-generation color e-paper technology for e-readers and e-notebooks: Kaleido 4. With its new design, E Ink Kaleido 4 supports a broader range of digital content. Compared to the previous generation, E Ink Kaleido 4 doubles its color gamut volume to more than 40K, increases white reflectance by 15%, and improves contrast by 50%. Additionally, with the introduction of new algorithms, E Ink Kaleido 4 is capable of video playback at up to 18 frames per second. These enhancements let color e-paper display text, images, charts, presentations, and video more clearly while reducing the perception of screen graininess.

As e-Paper applications continue to expand from e-Books to classroom and workplace environments, the content on the device is also becoming increasingly diverse, ranging from color PDFs, PowerPoint presentations, and data charts to educational illustrations, science and technology reference materials, and engineering drawings. Therefore, color e-Paper must better balance color, brightness, contrast, and clarity to convey information accurately.

E. INK has confirmed with Good e-Reader that the color resolution has been increased to 300 PPI, whereas Kaleido 3 could only do 150 PPI. This will dramatically increase the number of colors to make cover art, images, e-textbooks, PDF files have more contrast, look less grainy.

The first products to use Kaleido 4 is the Hanvon M10C IIl, but the prices and release date is unknown. The device will only be available in China. The M10C II pairs E Ink Kaleido 4 with Hanvon Technology’s OCR, voice and AI-powered office applications, along with features such as cloud library synchronization, ripple-reduction technology, responsive third-party app scaling and optimized font rendering. For handwriting, its wireless, battery-free digital pen offers 8,192 levels of pressure sensitivity, while a micro-etched tempered-glass surface reduces glare and parallax and further provides a paper-like writing resistance. Together, these capabilities create a smoother experience for reading, writing, note-taking and on-the-go productivity.

New Technology

    • Color gamut: More than 2× that of Kaleido 3
    • White reflectance: 15% improvement
    • Contrast ratio: 50% improvement
    • Graininess: Reduced through changes to the display structure
    • Display technology: Updated color filter, frontlight, and Oxide TFT backplane
    • Color Resolution: It looks like Kaleido 4 will be 300 PPI, instead of 150 PPI on Kaleido 3.

When will we see e-readers with Kaleido 4?

There likely won’t be very many new e-paper panels available until at least early 2027. This means a new Amazon Kindle Colorsoft, Kobo Libra Color Gen 2, Kobo Clara Color Gen 2, a color NOOK, or devices from vendors like Bigme, Onyx Boox, and Fujitsu will take a while. I do not expect any devices to start shipping to Canada, the United States, the UK, Australia, or Europe until Spring 2027.

entries.title: YouTube might offer Audiobooks in 2027
entries.summary: According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, YouTube is “looking” into audiobooks for a future addition to the app. The post YouTube might offer Audiobooks in 2027 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
YouTube is reportedly in talks with major book publishers to launch an official audiobook feature that could debut as early as 2027. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, Google is exploring ways to expand its ecosystem and is considering bundling the new feature into its existing YouTube Premium subscription, which currently costs $15.99 per month in the U.S.

There is a serious piracy problem on YouTube right now. There are a copious number of channels with audiobook videos on the platform if you look. Some feature public-domain titles, but others offer books that aren’t legally allowed on YouTube. The existing system to ensure a piece of work belongs to the uploader doesn’t really apply to audiobooks, so it’s the virtual Wild West.

Edison data shows that 45% of listeners have consumed an audiobook on YouTube (up from 35% previously), making it a major distribution channel—often filled with low-quality robotic voices. Similar pirated AI audiobooks also bleed into platforms like Spotify, disguised as podcasts.

YouTube will have its work cut out for it, since competition is already firmly entrenched. Spotify offers a variety of plans. Premium subscriptions include 15 hours of audiobook listening per month; for an additional $12 per month, you can add another 15 hours with the Audiobooks+ add-on. A standalone Audio Access plan is also available for $10 a month, which provides 15 hours each month. Additionally, individual audiobooks can be purchased through the Spotify Web Player.

On the other hand, Audible’s Standard membership costs $9 per month, granting you access to one audiobook each month from its collection as long as you maintain your subscription. For $15 a month, the Premium membership gives you one monthly credit for a title you can keep indefinitely, plus access to a vast catalog for unlimited listening.

Everand (formerly Scribd) offers a flat-fee monthly subscription, around $11.99 per month, providing unlimited-style access to audiobooks, eBooks, and magazines, though heavy use of trending titles can face throttling. Amazon Kindle Unlimited, Kobo Plus, and even the public library all offer audiobooks.

entries.title: US E-book revenue was down 5.7% in August 2026
entries.summary: E-book revenues were down 5.7% to $83.9 million for the month, and revenues from Digital Audiobooks were up 12.6% in August, coming in at $105.4 million. The post US E-book revenue was down 5.7% in August 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E-book revenues were down 5.7% to $83.9 million for the month, and revenues from Digital Audiobooks were up 12.6% in August, coming in at $105.4 million. Physical Audio revenues were down 35.2%, coming in at $400 thousand. Year-to-date E-Book revenues were down 3.4% compared to 2025, generating $685.1 million. Digital Audiobook revenue was up 12.6% to $806.3 million, while Physical Audio revenue was down 11.9% to $3.5 million.

In terms of physical formats during the month of August, Hardback revenues were up 13.8%, coming in at $320.2 million; Paperbacks were up 17.6%, with $333.3 million in revenue; Mass Market was down 14.6% to $6.2 million; and Special Bindings were up 3.7%, with $20.4 million in revenue.

Hardback revenues were up 3.1% year-to-date to $2.1 billion; Paperbacks were up 11.8% to $2.3 billion; Mass Market was down 57.2% to $26.9 million; and Special Bindings were up 14.5% to $152.6 million.

entries.title: Libro.fm e-books are pushed back until 2027
entries.summary: Libro.fm has admitted that their new e-book platform will not go live until 2027, but further details will be announced by the end of 2026. The post Libro.fm e-books are pushed back until 2027 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Libro.fm is an audiobook subscription platform that allows users to purchase audiobooks while financially supporting a designated local independent bookstore. The company has confirmed in a new FAQ that its new e-book platform will launch sometime in 2027, after initially saying it would be available in 2026.

They stated that “Our bookselling partners will gain access to ebooks this fall, and we’ll share updates on wider availability as we approach 2027. All of our audiobooks will remain DRM-free, and we are working to bring on as many DRM-free ebooks as possible. Unfortunately, publisher terms won’t always allow that. Access to DRM-free ebooks matters, and we promise not only to keep encouraging our publishing partners to offer DRM-free reads, but also to do what we can to make these books as accessible as possible in the meantime. Credits can be used to purchase audiobooks or ebooks. However, Ebooks can also be purchased à la carte.”

The company will also support a number of e-book readers. “We are working to make our ebooks as accessible as possible, which includes the ability to read them on different e-readers and apps. While we can’t confirm the extent of e-reader compatibility yet, we’ll share clear information as we near launch. The best reading experience, including features like LibroSync, will be available in the Libro apps.”

It would be nice if they added Kobo to the list, since many other companies are starting to work with them, such as the Cloud Library.
